s0.p35: The value **⟦f19⟧** means that the variable has no value. This value is inconsistent in the sense that such a value refers to primitive data types, while the **⟦f20⟧** operator returns ‘⟦f21⟧’. And all data of type ‘⟦f22⟧’ (except **⟦f23⟧**) is of **reference type**. This bug should be kept in mind when we use the **⟦f24⟧** operator.
s0.p36: Another peculiarity of **⟦f25⟧** value is that if you use strict equality, then **⟦f26⟧** will be equal only to itself, while non-strictly it will be equal only to **⟦f27⟧**. This is understandable: they have different data types. But the fact that the value of **⟦f28⟧** and the value of **⟦f29⟧** are considered equal (without regard to data type) tells us that both of these values have the same meaning: no value. Both of these values are primitives, and they have one more feature in common, which we will understand a bit later, when we start studying constructors.
